title: Desktop provider environment allowlist
implementation: Rewrote the Desktop built-in daemon spawn filter in apps/desktop/src/daemon/rust-daemon.ts: AIT_SERVER_* variables are stripped except a ten-name provider allowlist (CODEX, CLAUDE, ANTIGRAVITY, OPENCODE, DEEPSEEK_HARNESS, PI, OMP, MINIMAX_CODE _BIN plus DEEPSEEK_HARNESS_PROFILE and DEEPSEEK_HARNESS_TRANSPORT), matching provider composition (crates/provider/src/composition.rs) and the daemon CLI (bins/daemon/src/main.rs AIT_SERVER_OMP_BIN). Values pass through unchanged; token/address/data isolation and AIT_SERVER_HUB_NOTIFICATIONS behavior are untouched. Donor daemon-manager.ts/daemon-manager.test.ts hunks are DirectDownloadManager work owned by task01/26, not S1, and were not imported. Added targeted propagation/isolation tests to the existing rust-daemon-environment.test.ts and a real launcher interaction (rust-daemon-launch-environment.test.ts + fixtures/environment-daemon.cjs) that starts a child through RustDaemonManager.start(), completes the authenticated readiness handshake, and asserts the environment the child actually received. No Rust code or Rust tests changed. No new ADR: this is an environment passthrough contract within existing ADR-048/207 lifecycle ownership, documented in docs/operations/daemon.md and CHANGELOG.md.
acceptance: Tests cover all ten allowed names and representative forbidden variables (LISTEN, DATA_DIR, LOG_LEVEL, MCP_SOCKET, BIN, near-miss suffixes, unrelated secrets), preserve values, and match provider composition/daemon CLI consumers. Verified red/green: with the main strip-all filter restored, the propagation test and the launcher test fail; with the allowlist they pass. Actual launcher smoke ran on Linux (real child process, readiness handshake, SIGTERM stop). Old clients/hosts: no wire or storage change; older Desktop builds keep stripping all AIT_SERVER_*, so provider overrides only take effect after upgrading Desktop; standalone daemons are unaffected.
